newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN PROSECUTOR ARREST FORMER BANK CHAIRMAN.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN PROSECUTOR ARREST FORMER BANK CHAIRMAN.

text.p: The former head of Romania's leading state-run Bancorex bank was charged with embezzlement on Wednesday, his lawyer said.

Razvan Temesan, in police detention since Tuesday, is alleged by prosecutors to have used his position between 1992 and earlier this year to offer a string of companies and individuals the use of luxury cars belonging to the bank.
The prosecutors put the costs of repairs and maintenance equivalent to $83,000. He faces up to 15 years in prison if convicted.
Temesan's lawyer Bogdan Ionescu said his client was innocent of all charges and denounced his arrest as a "coup".

Police said they were also investigating allegations that Temesan had offered foreign exchange to more than 350 private companies at preferential rates until he was sacked by a shareholders' meeting last March.
Bancorex specialises in foreign trade financing and handles the bulk of foreign exchange trading on the local market. It is one of the most popular commercial banks in the country.

Reformist President Emil Constantinescu, who defeated an ex-communist in last November's election, has made the fight against corruption a priority in his bid to right the Balkan country's sagging economy and boost living standards.
Several prominent entrepreneurs have been put under investigation for corruption over the past months.
